Could you tell us about your educational background? I had my primary school in Niger State and then moved to Ogbomoso, Oyo State for my secondary school at Nurudeen Grammar School. I returned to Niger for my degree at Ibrahim Badamasi Babangida University (Pioneer), where I obtained my BSc degree in Chemistry. How did you become an actor? It has always been my dream to become an actor, and that started in my secondary school days. After graduating from the university, I still continued my life in Minna, but was thinking about how to relocate to Lagos to achieve my goals. Eventually, I came to Lagos in 2017 and joined the film industry in 2018. What were the challenges you encountered? Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources Every field has its challenges in one way or the other. One of the challenges of an up-and-coming actor is visibility. You need people who can trust you to deliver when given roles. What kept you going amid these challenges? First of all, it was God who gave me the strength to persist. And I mustered a lot of endurance and consistency, which are qualities needed to shine in the industry. Stop turning campaigns into entertainment shows, Nollywood actor tells politicians Before Stardom With… Victoria Adeboye Late Nollywood actor’s daughter begs AGN to remove burial poster Tell us about your character in The Herd? I played the role of Musa, the only Yoruba- and Hausa-speaking bandit character. I’m glad that The Herd won three awards out of its 10 nominations at the 22nd Africa Movie Academy Awards this past Sunday. Apart from acting, what other work ventures are you involved in? I’m a professional fashion designer who sews with or without taking customer measurements. Are you working on any project lately?
